scope: Theorem 5.1 (Collar extension) of the manuscript “Bounded scalar curvature and smooth extension of four-dimensional Ricci flow” (preprints/Bounded-scalar-curvature-and-smooth-extension-of-four-dimensional-Ricci-flow-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 351 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 95655c4053c94f2b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 37. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are σ∗ > 0, R∗ < ∞, and C < ∞, depending only on q, k, the fixed shell choices, and the weight comparison constants, with the following property. If σ ≤ σ∗ and R ≥ R∗, there is a metric h̄ on E such that ∥h̄ − δ∥Hk q ≤ C∥g − δ∥Hk(C1), ∥g − h̄∥Hk(C1) + ∥ Ric(h̄)∥Hk−2 q+2 ≤ Cm1. (5.4) The map g|C1 7→ h̄ − δ is real analytic on a fixed neighborhood of zero in collar Hk, and its first derivative into Hk q has uniformly bounded operator norm. It is independent of R, the weights, and the choice of an exterior realizing the collar data. There is also such an analytic extension ĥ, equal to g near the inner boundary, for which ∥ĥ − δ∥Hk q ≤ C∥g − δ∥Hk(C1), ∥ Ric(ĥ)∥Hk−2 q+2 ≤ Cm1, and whose first derivative has the same bound.
